title: Timers
summary: Delay, extend and shape signals in time with TON, TOF and TP, running on simulation time.
objectives: Choose between TON, TOF and TP

sections.heading: Time as a condition
sections.body: Timers are **function blocks** with memory. **TON** delays switching on, **TOF** delays switching off, **TP** produces a fixed pulse. You declare an instance and call it every scan.

sections.heading: TON timing diagram
sections.body: Q follows IN only after PT, and drops immediately.

sections.heading: Warning delay
sections.body: Light a warning lamp, then start the motor 3 s later.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Calling the timer only inside an IF branch. A timer must be called every scan, otherwise it never sees IN go FALSE and never resets.

question.question: A fan must keep running for 30 s after the heater switches off. Which timer?
question.explanation: TOF holds Q for PT after IN goes off.

sections.heading: Practice: delayed start
sections.body: Implement a 3 s warning before the conveyor starts.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
TON delays on, TOF delays off, TP makes pulses; call every instance once per scan.

**Troubleshooting note:** PLC Lab timers use simulation time: pausing the simulation pauses them, so you can step through a delay cycle by cycle.

checkpoint.question: What is ET of a TON while IN is FALSE?
checkpoint.explanation: TON resets when IN is FALSE.

checkpoint.question: Which literal means two and a half seconds?
checkpoint.explanation: IEC duration literals start with T#.
